claims.text: The starting NbMoTaW HEA is produced by conventional casting.
The as-cast NbMoTaW HEA possesses moderate inherent atomic disorder.
Controlled ball milling followed by consolidation increases atomic-level disorder in NbMoTaW.
Increased atomic-level disorder increases electron scattering in NbMoTaW.
Increased disorder changes the electron mean free path and scattering rate.
Under dirty-limit superconductivity, a moderate increase in disorder and scattering raises the upper critical field Hc2.
Pair-breaking caused by excessive disorder suppresses the superconducting critical temperature Tc.
Superconducting parameters depend non-monotonically on the level of disorder.
Ball-milled NbMoTaW samples will exhibit systematically higher Hc2 than as-cast samples.
At moderate disorder, Tc may remain similar to or become slightly higher than in the as-cast state.
At excessive disorder, Tc may become lower than in the as-cast state.
The proposed mechanism applies only while crystallinity is maintained and amorphization is avoided.
The proposed mechanism requires the absence of extrinsic contamination.
The proposed results are limited to similarly processed NbMoTaW measured below 10 K.
Residual resistivity can serve as an indicator of electron scattering and disorder.
Ball-milling duration can be varied to produce incrementally different disorder levels.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows Tc to remain similar at moderate disorder, but the falsification rule states that invariant Tc can falsify the hypothesis regardless of the measured increase in scattering. Thus, an explicitly permitted outcome is also designated as falsifying.
